subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this shared localization contract across runtime messages, Gateway errors, command and skill metadata, recipient locale ownership, and release completeness for the 21-locale baseline?
rationale: The proposal is technically coherent, but source inspection cannot authorize the cross-owner product policy, compatibility guarantees, and release-blocking semantics it establishes.

options.title: Sponsor and refine the RFC
options.body: Keep the draft open, resolve the five listed owner decisions and compatibility behavior, and then advance it through the RFC lifecycle.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Limit this RFC to locale resolution and runtime message descriptors, leaving metadata and release completeness to later proposals.

options.title: Decline the shared contract
options.body: Continue surface-specific localization without introducing a product-wide runtime and coverage contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and refine the RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open, resolve the five listed owner decisions and compatibility behavior, and then advance it through the RFC lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: A product-level OpenClaw owner is better positioned than an individual surface contributor to sponsor or narrow a cross-owner RFC.
